propositions: When no model-class table is configured, context-limit escalation of a provider-qualified primary (e.g. a Bedrock deployment) silently retargets the call to a bare Anthropic model id, crossing providers.
_rung_target decides escalation targets purely from MODEL_LADDER constants, never taking the run's actual model as input, so provider qualifiers on cfg.model are discarded.
The provider jump causes hard failures in provider-isolated containers or unbudgeted Anthropic spend, and occurs even on the common one-criterion retry before deep escalation.

The fix threads the primary model into _rung_target and applies a provider-agreement rule: same provider returns today's value, the primary's own rung stays on the primary verbatim, and unnameable higher rungs are dropped.
Dropping unnameable higher rungs must fail safe by stopping escalation and reporting the existing _too_big size-failure finding rather than crashing or crossing providers.
MODEL_LADDER and largest_window_tokens remain unchanged so escalation windows stay keyed on concrete model families while targets move to the class vocabulary, preserving byte-for-byte back-compat.
